multiple_choice_questions.question: When using AI to handle critical matters (e.g., financial calculations, legal advice), you usually:
options: A. Trust it completely and use the results directly.
B. Remain skeptical and manually verify every single data point.
C. Use it only as a reference; the final version is rewritten by yourself.

multiple_choice_questions.question: When the AI speaks in a very confident tone (e.g., "I am certain..."), your level of trust:
options: A. Increases significantly; I feel it is more sure of itself.
B. Remains unchanged; tone does not equate to accuracy.
C. Triggers a sense of vigilance; I worry it is masking a potential hallucination.

multiple_choice_questions.question: If the AI makes a mistake on a minor issue, your trust in its ability to handle subsequent complex problems:
options: A. Collapses instantly; I view the entire system as unreliable.
B. Drops slightly; I will check its output more frequently.
C. Is largely unaffected; I consider local errors to be a matter of probability.

multiple_choice_questions.question: Are you willing to provide personal private data (e.g., diaries, undisclosed projects) to the AI for analysis?
options: A. Very willing; I trust the platform's privacy protection protocols.
B. Provide it selectively, removing extremely sensitive information.
C. Never; I do not trust the security of AI services.

multiple_choice_questions.question: Regarding AI-generated code, your workflow is:
options: A. Run it directly; if it throws an error, ask the AI to fix it.
B. Carefully read every line of logic to ensure there are no backdoors or low-level bugs.
C. Only copy the core algorithm and manually integrate it into my own architecture.

multiple_choice_questions.question: In a Generative UI scenario, if the AI automatically fills out a form for you, you would:
options: A. Glance at key items and submit if there are no major issues.
B. Click and check item by item, even comparing it with the original data.
C. Consider this automation unreliable; clear it and fill it out manually.

multiple_choice_questions.question: When faced with a decision recommendation from AI (e.g., "You should choose Option A"), you:
options: A. Tend to adopt it, believing the AI's analysis is more objective than mine.
B. Use it only as an alternative; I trust my intuition and experience more.
C. Require it to list all the disadvantages of Option A, otherwise I won't trust it.

multiple_choice_questions.question: When the AI cannot answer a question and proactively admits "I don't know," your trust in it:
options: A. Increases; I find it honest and aware of its boundaries.
B. Decreases; I feel its capability is limited and it isn't "smart" enough.
C. No feeling; it's just a standard programmed response.

multiple_choice_questions.question: If the AI consistently performs stably and efficiently, do you develop a sense of "dependency"?
options: A. Yes; I feel I can't do without it, and may even lose the motivation for independent thinking.
B. No; I always view it as an auxiliary tool and can switch back to manual mode at any time.
C. Occasionally; especially when I am exhausted or in a rush to deliver a task.

multiple_choice_questions.question: In a collaborative task, if a colleague says, "This was written by AI," you would:
options: A. Automatically lower the trust weight of the document.
B. Raise expectations, assuming the logic should be tighter than human work.
C. Keep evaluation standards the same, looking only at the quality of the content itself.
